surface_mechanism_description: The reaction of tin(IV) chloride with hydrogen sulfide under APCVD conditions produced yellow films that analyzed as SnS2. At lower temperatures SnS2 films are produced whilst at 545 °C SnS films are formed. The reason for this changeover in film composition is not entirely clear as both SnS and SnS2 have decomposition points above 800 °C. Thus it is unlikely that the SnS is obtained by thermal decomposition of SnS2.
